content:
iPhone Ultra is set to be released next month, and the latest leaks suggest the device's front camera may be placed in an unusual location.

Both front-facing cameras on the iPhone Ultra could be located in the corners of the screen rather than centered.

When the iPhone Ultra arrives, it will be Apple's first attempt at a foldable iPhone. As such, the device will differ from a "normal" iPhone design in several ways, including its camera arrangement.

The iPhone Ultra is said to feature two rear cameras — a main lens and an ultra-wide lens — plus two front-facing cameras.

It has two front-facing cameras because the foldable will have two screens: an outer screen and a larger one that appears when unfolded.

Until now, we'd expected the outer screen's front camera to be placed in the middle. But according to the latest leak, the camera position could be even more unusual.

A third-party screen protector circulating online appears to show a camera cut-out in the top-right corner of the outer screen and the top-left corner of the inner screen.

Accessory makers may well have guessed wrong. Like everyone else, they're just speculating. But if this leak turns out to be true, it would represent a major shift in front camera placement.

Apple has always placed the selfie camera in the top center of the iPhone. Moving it to a corner would likely mean that in many selfies — especially group shots — users wouldn't be looking at the camera.

It actually makes more sense not to center the inner screen's camera, since the crease area simply can't accommodate a lens, and users will likely use the outer screen for selfies. But if even the outer screen's camera isn't centered, users may need some time to adjust.

If Apple moves the iPhone Ultra's front cameras to the corners, do you think that'll be a problem? Share your thoughts in the comments.
